verses.1:1: Now it happened in the days of Ahasuerus, the very Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Cush over one hundred twenty-seven provinces,
verses.1:2: in those days, as King Ahasuerus sat on his royal throne, which was in Susa the citadel,
verses.1:3: in the third year of his reign he gave a banquet for all his officials and his servants; the army of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the officials of the provinces were before him
verses.1:4: as he displayed the riches of the glory of his kingdom and the splendor of the majesty of his greatness for many days, one hundred eighty days.
verses.1:5: When these days were completed, the king gave a seven-day banquet for all the people present in Susa the citadel, from greatest to least, in the courtyard of the garden of the king's pavilion.
verses.1:6: Hangings of white cotton and violet were secured with cords of fine linen and purple onto silver rings and pillars of white marble; couches of gold and silver stood upon a pavement of porphyry, white marble, mother-of-pearl, and dark stone.
verses.1:7: Drinks were served in golden vessels, each vessel differing from the next, and royal wine was abundant, in keeping with the king's bounty.
verses.1:8: And the drinking followed the law, with no one compelling another, for so the king had directed every chief officer of his house, to act according to each man's wish.
verses.1:9: Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace belonging to King Ahasuerus.
verses.1:10: On the seventh day, when the king's heart was glad with wine, he ordered Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven eunuchs who attended in the presence of King Ahasuerus,
verses.1:11: to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing the royal crown, in order to show the peoples and the officials her beauty, for she was lovely in appearance.
verses.1:12: Yet Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's word conveyed by the eunuchs. Then the king grew intensely angry, and his fury burned within him.
verses.1:13: Then the king spoke to the wise men who knew the times, for that was the king's procedure before all who knew law and justice,
verses.1:14: and those nearest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and sat first in the kingdom:
verses.1:15: "According to the law, what is to be done with Queen Vashti, because she has not carried out the command of King Ahasuerus conveyed by the eunuchs?"
verses.1:16: Then Memucan said in the presence of the king and the officials, "Queen Vashti has not wronged the king alone, but also all the officials and all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.
verses.1:17: For the queen's conduct will go out to all the women, making their husbands despised in their eyes as they say, 'King Ahasuerus commanded that Queen Vashti be brought before him, yet she did not come.'
verses.1:18: This very day the noble ladies of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen's conduct will speak out to all the king's officials, and there will be plenty of contempt and anger.
verses.1:19: If it pleases the king, let a royal order go out from his presence, and let it be written among the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be repealed, that Vashti is not to come before King Ahasuerus, and let the king give her royal position to another who is better than she.
verses.1:20: When the decree that the king makes is heard throughout all his kingdom, vast though it is, all the women will give honor to their husbands, from greatest to least."
verses.1:21: This proposal was pleasing in the eyes of the king and the officials, and the king acted according to the word of Memucan.
verses.1:22: He sent letters to all the king's provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, that every man should rule in his own household and speak in the language of his own people.
verses.2:1: After these events, when the fury of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti, both what she had done and what had been decreed against her.
verses.2:2: Then the king's young men who attended him said, "Let young virgin women who are lovely in appearance be sought for the king.
verses.2:3: And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, so that they may gather every young virgin woman who is lovely in appearance to Susa the citadel, to the house of the women, under the charge of Hegai, the king's eunuch, keeper of the women; and let their cosmetic treatments be given to them.
verses.2:4: Then let the young woman who is pleasing in the king's eyes reign as queen in place of Vashti." This proposal was pleasing in the king's eyes, and he did so.
verses.2:5: There was a Jewish man in Susa the citadel whose name was Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,
verses.2:6: who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem among the exiles who were exiled with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had exiled.
verses.2:7: He was raising Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. Now the young woman was beautiful in form and lovely in appearance, and when her father and her mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.
verses.2:8: So it happened, when the king's order and his law were heard and when many young women were gathered to Susa the citadel under the charge of Hegai, that Esther was taken into the king's palace, under the charge of Hegai, keeper of the women.
verses.2:9: The young woman was pleasing in his eyes and won kindness before him, so he hurried to supply her with her cosmetic treatments and her portions, as well as the seven suitable young women to be given to her from the king's palace, and he moved her and her young women to the best part of the house of the women.
verses.2:10: Esther did not disclose her people or her ancestry, for Mordecai had commanded her not to disclose it.
verses.2:11: Every single day Mordecai walked back and forth in front of the courtyard of the house of the women to learn of Esther's well-being and what was being done with her.
verses.2:12: Now when each young woman's turn arrived to go in to King Ahasuerus, at the end of her twelve months under the regulation for the women—for that was how the days of their purifying treatments were completed, six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and cosmetic treatments for the women—
verses.2:13: in this manner the young woman would go in to the king: whatever she asked for would be given to her to take with her from the house of the women to the king's palace.
verses.2:14: In the evening she would go in, and in the morning she would return to the second house of the women, under the charge of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch, keeper of the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and she was summoned by name.
verses.2:15: Now when the turn arrived for Esther, daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her as his own daughter, to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai, the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, advised. And Esther kept winning favor in the eyes of all who saw her.
verses.2:16: So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, into his royal palace, in the tenth month, which is the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.2:17: And the king loved Esther more than all the women, and she won favor and kindness before him more than all the virgins; so he placed the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
verses.2:18: Then the king gave a great banquet for all his officials and his servants, Esther's banquet; he also granted relief to the provinces and distributed gifts in keeping with the king's bounty.
verses.2:19: Now when virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
verses.2:20: Esther still did not disclose her ancestry or her people, just as Mordecai had commanded her; for Esther kept carrying out Mordecai's command, just as when she was being raised by him.
verses.2:21: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs from among the guards of the threshold, grew angry and sought to lay a hand on King Ahasuerus.
verses.2:22: The matter became known to Mordecai, and he told Queen Esther, and Esther reported it to the king in Mordecai's name.
verses.2:23: When the matter was investigated and found to be so, both of them were hanged on a wooden pole. And this was written in the book of the chronicles in the king's presence.
verses.3:1: After these events, King Ahasuerus promoted Haman, son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and elevated him, placing his seat above all the officials who were with him.
verses.3:2: And all the king's servants who were at the king's gate were kneeling and bowing low to Haman, for so the king had commanded concerning him. Yet Mordecai would neither kneel nor bow low.
verses.3:3: Then the king's servants who were at the king's gate said to Mordecai, "Why are you transgressing the king's command?"
verses.3:4: Now it happened, as they spoke to him day after day and he would not listen to them, that they reported it to Haman to see whether Mordecai's words would stand, for he had told them that he was a Jew.
verses.3:5: When Haman saw that Mordecai was neither kneeling nor bowing low to him, Haman was filled with fury.
verses.3:6: Yet in his eyes he disdained to lay a hand on Mordecai alone, since they had told him of Mordecai's people; so Haman sought to destroy all the Jews who were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai.
verses.3:7: In the first month, which is the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day and from month to month, to the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.
verses.3:8: Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people scattered and separated among the peoples throughout all the provinces of your kingdom. Their laws differ from those of every people, and they do not keep the king's laws, so it does not profit the king to leave them alone.
verses.3:9: If it pleases the king, let it be written to annihilate them, and I will weigh out ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who carry out the business, to bring into the king's treasuries."
verses.3:10: Then the king removed his signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman, son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the adversary of the Jews.
verses.3:11: And the king said to Haman, "The silver is given to you, and the people also, to do with them as is good in your eyes."
verses.3:12: Then the king's scribes were summoned in the first month, on its thirteenth day, and everything Haman commanded was written to the king's satraps, to the governors over each province, and to the officials of each people, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language; it was written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with the king's signet ring.
verses.3:13: Letters were dispatched by couriers to all the king's provinces to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate all the Jews, from young to old, little children and women, on a single day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, and to plunder their possessions.
verses.3:14: A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province, made public to all the peoples, so that they would be ready for that day.
verses.3:15: The couriers set out in haste at the king's word, and the law was issued in Susa the citadel. The king and Haman sat down to drink, while the city of Susa was bewildered.
verses.4:1: Now Mordecai learned everything that had been done, and Mordecai tore his garments and put on sackcloth and ashes. Then he went out into the middle of the city and cried out a great and bitter cry.
verses.4:2: He came up to the front of the king's gate, for no one was allowed to enter the king's gate in sackcloth attire.
verses.4:3: In every single province, wherever the king's command and his decree reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and wailing; and sackcloth and ashes were spread out for many.
verses.4:4: Then Esther's female attendants and her eunuchs came and told her, and the queen was greatly anguished. She sent garments to clothe Mordecai and to remove his sackcloth from him, but he would not accept them.
verses.4:5: So Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs whom he had stationed before her, and instructed him concerning Mordecai, to find out what this was and what it was about.
verses.4:7: And Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, as well as the exact sum of silver that Haman had promised to weigh out into the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.
verses.4:8: He also gave him a copy of the written decree that had been issued in Susa to annihilate them, to show Esther and inform her, and to charge her to go in to the king to implore his favor and to appeal before him on behalf of her people.
verses.4:9: Then Hathach came and reported Mordecai's words to Esther.
verses.4:10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and gave him instructions for Mordecai:
verses.4:11: "All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that for any man or woman who goes in to the king into the inner courtyard without being summoned, there is one law: to be put to death, except the one to whom the king extends the gold scepter so that he may live. Yet I myself have not been summoned to go in to the king these thirty days."
verses.4:12: So they reported Esther's words to Mordecai.
verses.4:13: Then Mordecai gave orders to reply to Esther, "Do not imagine within yourself that in the king's house you will escape more than all the Jews.
verses.4:14: For if you keep completely silent at this time, relief and rescue will arise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. And who knows whether it was for a time like this that you reached royalty?"
verses.4:15: Then Esther gave orders to reply to Mordecai:
verses.4:16: "Go, assemble all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast on my behalf; do not eat and do not drink for three days, night and day. I and my female attendants will also fast in the same way. And then I will go in to the king, which is not according to the law; and should I perish, I perish."
verses.4:17: Then Mordecai went on his way and did according to everything Esther had charged him.
verses.5:1: Now it happened on the third day that Esther put on royal attire and stood in the inner courtyard of the king's palace, facing the king's palace, while the king was sitting on his royal throne in the royal palace, facing the entrance of the palace.
verses.5:2: When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard, she gained favor in his eyes, and the king extended to Esther the gold scepter that was in his hand. So Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter.
verses.5:3: Then the king said to her, "What is the matter, Queen Esther, and what is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be granted to you."
verses.5:4: Esther said, "If it seems good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him."
verses.5:5: Then the king said, "Hurry Haman here, to carry out Esther's word." So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.5:6: And the king said to Esther during the wine banquet, "What is your petition? It will be granted to you. And what is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be done."
verses.5:7: Esther answered and said, "My petition and my request:
verses.5:8: If I have found favor in the eyes of the king, and if it seems good to the king to grant my petition and to carry out my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do according to the king's word."
verses.5:9: So Haman went out on that day joyful and cheerful at heart. Yet when Haman saw Mordecai at the king's gate, that he neither stood up nor trembled at his presence, Haman was filled with fury against Mordecai.
verses.5:10: Yet Haman held himself in check and went to his house. Then he sent and brought his friends and his wife Zeresh.
verses.5:11: And Haman recounted to them the splendor of his wealth, the great number of his sons, all the ways the king had magnified him, and how he had exalted him above the officials and the king's servants.
verses.5:12: And Haman said, "Furthermore, Queen Esther brought no one with the king to the banquet she had prepared except me, and for tomorrow also I am invited by her along with the king.
verses.5:13: Yet all of this counts for nothing to me whenever I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."
verses.5:14: Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Let them make a wooden pole fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king so that they may hang Mordecai on it; then go joyfully with the king to the banquet." The proposal seemed good to Haman, and he made the wooden pole.
verses.6:1: On that night, the king's sleep fled, and he gave orders to bring the book of records, the chronicles, and they were being read before the king.
verses.6:2: And it was found written how Mordecai had reported concerning Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs from among the guards of the threshold, who had sought to stretch out a hand against King Ahasuerus.
verses.6:3: Then the king said, "What honor and distinction has been done for Mordecai because of this?" And the king's attendants who served him said, "Not a thing has been done for him."
verses.6:4: So the king said, "Who is in the courtyard?" Now Haman had come into the outer courtyard of the king's palace to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the wooden pole that he had prepared for him.
verses.6:5: The king's attendants said to him, "Look, Haman is standing in the courtyard." And the king said, "Let him come in."
verses.6:6: So Haman came in, and the king said to him, "What should be done for the man in whose honor the king delights?" Now Haman said in his heart, "To whom would the king delight to show honor more than to me?"
verses.6:7: Then Haman said to the king, "For a man in whose honor the king delights,
verses.6:8: let them bring a royal robe that the king has worn, and a horse that the king has ridden and on whose head a royal crown has been set.
verses.6:9: And let the robe and the horse be placed in the hand of one of the king's noble officials, and let them clothe the man in whose honor the king delights, and have him ride on the horse through the city square, and proclaim before him, 'This is how it shall be done for the man in whose honor the king delights.'"
verses.6:10: Then the king said to Haman, "Hurry, take the robe and the horse, just as you have spoken, and do so for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Do not leave out a single thing from all that you have spoken."
verses.6:11: So Haman took the robe and the horse, and clothed Mordecai, and had him ride through the city square, and proclaimed before him, "This is how it shall be done for the man in whose honor the king delights."
verses.6:12: Then Mordecai returned to the king's gate, while Haman hurried to his house, mourning, his head covered.
verses.6:13: And Haman recounted to his wife Zeresh and to all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his wise men and his wife Zeresh said to him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of the offspring of the Jews, you will not prevail against him, but you will certainly fall before him."
verses.6:14: While they were still speaking with him, the king's eunuchs arrived and rushed to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.7:1: Then the king and Haman came to drink with Queen Esther.
verses.7:2: On the second day also, at the wine banquet, the king said to Esther, "What is your petition, Queen Esther? It will be given to you. And what is your request? Up to half the kingdom, it will be done."
verses.7:3: Then Queen Esther answered and said, "If I have found favor in your eyes, King, and if it seems good to the king, let my life be given to me as my petition, and my people as my request.
verses.7:4: For we have been sold, I and my people, to be exterminated, to be killed, and to be destroyed. Now if we had been sold as male and female slaves, I would have kept silent, for the distress would not be worth the harm to the king."
verses.7:5: Then King Ahasuerus spoke and said to Queen Esther, "Who is he, and where is he, whose heart has emboldened him to do so?"
verses.7:6: And Esther said, "An adversary and an enemy—this wicked Haman!" Then Haman was gripped with terror before the king and the queen.
verses.7:7: The king rose in his fury from the wine banquet and went into the palace garden, while Haman remained to plead for his life with Queen Esther, for he saw that disaster had been determined against him by the king.
verses.7:8: When the king returned from the palace garden to the hall of the wine banquet, Haman was falling onto the couch where Esther was. And the king said, "Will he even assault the queen with me in the house?" As the word left the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.
verses.7:9: Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs before the king, said, "Moreover, look, the wooden pole that Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke good concerning the king, is standing at Haman's house, fifty cubits high." And the king said, "Hang him on it!"
verses.7:10: So they hanged Haman on the wooden pole that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king's fury subsided.
verses.8:1: On that day King Ahasuerus gave to Queen Esther the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he was to her.
verses.8:2: Then the king took off his signet ring, which he had taken away from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
verses.8:3: Then Esther spoke again before the king, fell at his feet, wept, and pleaded with him to avert the evil of Haman the Agagite and his plot that he had plotted against the Jews.
verses.8:4: The king held out the golden scepter to Esther. So Esther rose and stood before the king.
verses.8:5: And she said, "If it seems good to the king, and if I have found favor before him, and the matter seems proper before the king, and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to revoke the letters, the plot of Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews who are in all the king's provinces.
verses.8:6: For how can I bear to look upon the disaster that will overtake my people? And how can I bear to look upon the destruction of my relatives?"
verses.8:7: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "Look, I have given the house of Haman to Esther, and they have hanged him on the wooden pole because he stretched out his hand against the Jews.
verses.8:8: Now you yourselves write concerning the Jews whatever seems good in your eyes, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's signet ring; for a document that is written in the king's name and sealed with the king's signet ring cannot be revoked."
verses.8:9: So the king's scribes were summoned at that time, in the third month, that is, the month of Sivan, on its twenty-third day; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the satraps, the governors, and the officials of the provinces from India to Cush, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, and to the Jews in their own script and in their own language.
verses.8:10: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king's signet ring, and sent letters by couriers on horses, riding royal steeds, the offspring of stud mares,
verses.8:11: by which the king allowed the Jews who were in every city to assemble and to defend their lives, to exterminate, to kill, and to destroy any armed force of any people or province that would attack them, children and women, and to plunder their spoil,
verses.8:12: on a single day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, that is, the month of Adar.
verses.8:13: A copy of the document was to be issued as an edict in every province and made public to all the peoples, so that the Jews would be ready for that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
verses.8:14: The couriers, riding the royal steeds, went out hurried and pressed onward by the king's command. And the edict was issued in the citadel of Susa.
verses.8:15: Then Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, with a large golden crown and a cloak of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa cheered and rejoiced.
verses.8:16: To the Jews came light and gladness, joy and honor.
verses.8:17: And in every single province and in every single city, wherever the king's command and his edict arrived, there was gladness and joy for the Jews, a banquet and a festive day. And many from the peoples of the land declared themselves Jews, because the dread of the Jews had fallen upon them.
verses.9:1: Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month of Adar, on its thirteenth day, when the king's command and his edict were about to be carried out, on the day when the enemies of the Jews had hoped to gain mastery over them, the reverse happened, so that the Jews themselves gained mastery over those who hated them.
verses.9:2: The Jews assembled in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to lay hands on those who sought their harm. And no one stood before them, for the dread of them had fallen upon all the peoples.
verses.9:3: And all the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those who did the king's business were supporting the Jews, because the dread of Mordecai had fallen upon them.
verses.9:4: For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his fame spread throughout all the provinces, for the man Mordecai kept growing greater.
verses.9:6: And in the citadel of Susa the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
verses.9:7: And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
verses.9:8: and Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
verses.9:9: and Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vaizatha—
verses.9:10: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the adversary of the Jews—they killed; but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
verses.9:11: On that day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa came before the king.
verses.9:12: And the king said to Queen Esther, "In the citadel of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? Now what is your petition? It will be given to you. And what is your further request? It will be done."
verses.9:13: Then Esther said, "If it seems good to the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Susa tomorrow also to act according to today's edict, and let them hang the ten sons of Haman on the wooden pole."
verses.9:14: So the king commanded that this be done. An edict was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
verses.9:15: The Jews who were in Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
verses.9:16: Now the rest of the Jews who were in the king's provinces assembled and defended their lives, and gained rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them; but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
verses.9:17: This took place on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on its fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of banqueting and gladness.
verses.9:18: But the Jews who were in Susa assembled on its thirteenth day and on its fourteenth day, and on its fifteenth day they rested and made it a day of banqueting and gladness.
verses.9:19: Therefore the rural Jews, who live in the unwalled towns, observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as a day of gladness and banqueting, a festive day, and for sending food portions to one another.
verses.9:20: Then Mordecai wrote down these things and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far,
verses.9:21: establishing for them that they should observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and its fifteenth day every single year,
verses.9:22: as the days on which the Jews rested from their enemies, and as the month that was turned for them from sorrow into gladness and from mourning into a festive day, to make them days of banqueting and gladness, and of sending food portions to one another and gifts to the needy.
verses.9:23: So the Jews accepted what they had begun to do and what Mordecai had written to them.
verses.9:24: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the adversary of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to crush them and to destroy them.
verses.9:25: But when it came before the king, he commanded in writing that his wicked plot, which he had plotted against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and they hanged him and his sons on the wooden pole.
verses.9:26: Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and what they had seen concerning this matter, and what had come upon them,
verses.9:27: the Jews established and accepted upon themselves, upon their descendants, and upon all who joined themselves to them, without fail, to keep observing these two days according to what was written for them and at their appointed time every single year.
verses.9:28: And these days are to be remembered and observed throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and these days of Purim will not pass away from among the Jews, nor will their remembrance come to an end among their descendants.
verses.9:29: Then Queen Esther daughter of Abihail and Mordecai the Jew wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.
verses.9:31: to establish these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and just as they had established for themselves and for their descendants the matters of the fasts and their outcry.
verses.9:32: And the command of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.
verses.10:1: And King Ahasuerus placed a tax on the land and the coastlands of the sea.
verses.10:2: And all the deeds of his power and his might, and the detailed account of the greatness of Mordecai, whom the king made great, are they not written down in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
verses.10:3: For Mordecai the Jew was second to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and favored by the multitude of his brothers, seeking good for his people and speaking peace for all his offspring.

notes.1:6: The Hebrew fabric term karpas, a hapax legomenon of Indo-Iranian origin, denotes fine cotton. Several of the mosaic pavement terms (bahat, dar, and soheret) are also unique in Biblical Hebrew and are rendered approximately as porphyry, mother-of-pearl, and dark stone.
notes.1:7: The idiom 'in keeping with the king's bounty' translates the literal Hebrew 'according to the hand of the king' (also in 2:18). 'Drinks were served' renders the Hiphil infinitive construct of 'give to drink' used substantivally.
notes.1:16: Ketiv reads 'Mumcan'; Qere reads 'Memucan', matching the spelling in 1:14 and 1:21.
notes.1:22: The closing clause translates the Masoretic Hebrew literally ('and speaking in the language of his own people'), an unusual phrase often understood as asserting the husband's linguistic authority in a mixed-language household.
notes.2:3: The Masoretic Text spells the eunuch's name 'Hege' here, whereas 2:8 and 2:15 spell it 'Hegai'; both refer to the same official. The final clause uses a Qal infinitive absolute ('giving') with jussive force.
notes.2:18: The Hebrew hapax legomenon hanahah (from the root meaning 'to rest/grant rest') denotes relief or release, variously understood as a public holiday or a remission of taxes and compulsory service.
notes.2:23: 'Wooden pole' translates Hebrew ets (literally 'wood' or 'tree'), referring in Persian penal practice to a wooden stake for impalement or a gallows.
notes.3:4: Ketiv reads 'in their speaking' (be'omram); Qere reads 'as they spoke' (ke'omram), a minor orthographic difference with essentially the same temporal sense.
notes.3:7: The Masoretic Hebrew reads elliptically 'from day to day and from month to the twelfth month' (with an impersonal Hiphil verb 'one cast' for 'they cast'), indicating that the casting of the lot (pur, an Akkadian loanword) progressed through the calendar up to the twelfth month, Adar.
notes.3:13: 'Letters were dispatched' renders a Niphal infinitive absolute (nishloah) functioning as a finite passive verb, a stylistic feature of Late Biblical Hebrew.
notes.4:3: The Hophal imperfect yutsa (from yatsa, 'spread out') literally describes sackcloth and ashes being spread out beneath mourners as bedding (cf. Isaiah 14:11; 58:5).
notes.4:4: Qere reads wattavo'nah ('and they came'), normalizing the orthographic Ketiv spelling; both have the same meaning. The verb wattitchalchal ('was greatly anguished') is a unique Hithpalpel form of chul/chil ('writhe, tremble in anguish').
notes.4:7: Qere reads bayyehudim ('for the Jews'), normalizing the Ketiv's lengthened gentilic plural spelling; parashat ('exact sum', also in 10:2) denotes a precise specification.
notes.4:16: Literally 'and as I perish, I perish' (we-kha-asher avadti avadti), a Hebrew idiom of resolute acceptance using repeated Qal perfects (cf. Genesis 43:14).
notes.5:1: Literally 'put on royalty' (wattilbash Ester malkhut), an elliptical expression for royal robes or attire.
notes.5:7: Hebrew opens with an abrupt suspended subject ('My petition and my request') that builds suspense before Esther completes her thought with the conditional clauses in verse 8.
notes.5:14: Hebrew ets literally means 'wood' or 'tree,' here referring to a tall wooden stake or pole (fifty cubits, about 75 feet) for public hanging or impalement.
notes.6:1: Hebrew nadedah shenat hammelekh literally personifies sleep as fleeing, and the periphrastic construction wayyihyu niqra'im (Qal wayyiqtol of hayah plus Niphal participle of qara) conveys continuous action ('were being read').
notes.6:8: The relative clause 'and on whose head a royal crown has been set' (wa-asher nittan keter malkhut be-ro'sho, Niphal perfect of natan) syntactically parallels the preceding clause modifying the horse, reflecting royal Persian horse ornaments; verse 9 likewise specifies only the robe and the horse for the honoree.
notes.6:9: The Qal infinitive absolute we-naton ('and let ... be placed') functions jussively, a characteristic Late Biblical Hebrew construction in Esther; happartemim ('noble') is an Old Persian loanword denoting the highest-ranking nobles.
notes.6:13: The pairing of the Qal infinitive absolute with the imperfect (nafol tippol, 'you will certainly fall') intensifies the certainty of Haman's downfall.
notes.7:4: The final clause is a noted Hebrew crux: the noun hatzar can mean either "the distress" or "the adversary," and nezeq (a late Hebrew/Aramaic loanword) means "harm, damage, or loss," yielding either "the distress would not be worth the harm to the king" or "the adversary could not compensate for the king's loss."
notes.7:5: Hebrew idiom "whose heart has filled him to do so" (Qal perfect of male), expressing bold presumption. The Masoretic Text also repeats the verb "said" ("spoke and said") for dramatic emphasis.
notes.7:9: Hebrew ha'etz literally means "the wood" or "the tree," here referring to the fifty-cubit-high wooden stake or gallows Haman erected for execution and public display.
notes.8:1: Here and in 8:7, 8:13, 9:15, and 9:18, the written ketiv spells "the Jews" with a double yod (hayyehudiyyim), while the read qere simplifies the form to hayyehudim, with no change in meaning.
notes.8:10: The rare Persian loanwords achashteranim ("royal") and rammakim (hapax legomenon, "stud mares" or "breeding herds") underscore the elite speed of the imperial postal relay.
notes.8:13: The ketiv reads atudim and the qere reads atidim, orthographic variants of the adjective meaning "ready" or "prepared."
notes.8:17: The verb mityahadim is a hapax legomenon Hithpael participle derived from the gentilic "Jew," meaning either "declared themselves Jews" or "became Jews." Also, "a festive day" literally translates Hebrew yom tov ("a good day").
notes.9:1: Hebrew venahafoch hu uses a Niphal infinitive absolute of haphach ("turn, overturn") with the pronoun hu, literally "and it was overturned," emphasizing the complete reversal.
notes.9:16: As in 8:8, 9:6, 9:12, and 9:17-18, Late Biblical Hebrew frequently continues a finite verb with a chain of infinitives absolute (here Qal amod, noach, and harog) functioning as past-tense narrative verbs.
notes.9:19: The ketiv reads happeruzim and the qere reads happerazim, variant plural forms meaning "rural dwellers" or "inhabitants of unwalled towns," matching perazot ("unwalled towns") in the same clause.
notes.9:25: The feminine suffix in bevo'ah ("when it came" or "when she came") may refer either to the matter of Haman's plot (feminine machashavah) or to Esther herself. Hebrew im-hassepher literally reads "with the letter," meaning by written order.
notes.9:27: The ketiv reads the singular Piel perfect veqibbel ("and accepted," treating "the Jews" collectively as in 9:23), whereas the qere reads the plural veqibbelu ("and they accepted") in agreement with the preceding plural qiyyemu.
notes.10:1: The ketiv writes the king's name defectively without its two waws (אחשרש), while the qere reads the standard spelling אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ ("Ahasuerus"). The noun מַס denotes forced labor in earlier Hebrew, but in this Late Biblical Hebrew context it refers to a tax or tribute.
notes.10:2: The Piel verb גִּדְּלוֹ ("made him great") plays on the cognate noun גְּדֻלָּה ("greatness") here and the adjective גָּדוֹל ("great") in 10:3; the relative clause אֲשֶׁר גִּדְּלוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ may also be rendered "to which the king elevated him." The phrase סֵפֶר דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים is literally "the book of the events of the days," denoting royal chronicles or annals.
notes.10:3: The Qal passive participle רָצוּי ("favored, accepted") pairs with רֹב אֶחָיו, which denotes "the multitude of his brothers" and can also be understood as "the majority of his brothers." The Qal active participle phrase וְדֹבֵר שָׁלוֹם לְכׇל־זַרְעוֹ literally means "speaking peace for [or to] all his seed/offspring," referring to advocating the peace and welfare of all his descendants or wider kin.

unplaced.text: Then Hathach went out to Mordecai, to the city's public square in front of the king's gate.
So the Jews struck all their enemies with blows of the sword, with slaughter and destruction, and did to those who hated them as they wished.
He sent letters to all the Jews, to the one hundred twenty-seven provinces of the realm of Ahasuerus—words of peace and truth.
unplaced.note: The Hebrew verb is masculine singular, referring to Mordecai.
